newsitem.title: UK: US stocks in London up, trade thin ahead of Easter.
newsitem.headline: US stocks in London up, trade thin ahead of Easter.

text.p: U.S. shares were mostly higher on Thursday but trading volumes were light as most European participants were absent ahead of the Easter holiday break.
Wall Street is closed on Friday but will reopen for business on Monday, May 31.
"The market tone is a bit better but it has been very quiet this morning. Most of our clients, especially on the (European) continent have taken the day off," one market maker said.
"We've seen a bit of follow-through buying in some of the high-techs so we might see the Dow start higher today."

The Dow Industrials rose just 4.53 points to 6,880.70 on Wednesday, helped by big moves in IBM Corp and Exxon Corp - the two shares worth 24 points to the top-30 share index, according to data from Reuters Securities 3000.
"If you strip out IBM and Exxon, the Dow would have finished lower," the market maker said. But a solid performance by high-technology issues lifted the Nasdaq Composite 21.02 points to 1,269.08.
"Nasdaq was due for a bounce but the trend for second-liners is still down," another dealer said.
IBM, which rose $4-1/2 on Wednesday, was up $1/4 to $140-7/8 while Digital Corp added $1/8 to $29-1/2.
Intel Corp, which rose $7-3/8 on Wednesday, was down $1/8 to $140-1/2.

Motorola, another big gainer on Wednesday, was down $1 to $61 after the company repeated that it expected a year-on-year decline in quarterly earnings to persist until later this year, despite a modest recovery in its key semiconductor business.

Philip Morris slipped $1/2 to $118-7/8 after news that a Mississippi judge had ruled that internal documents from Liggett Group could be turned over to plaintiffs in a $650 million second-hand smoke lawsuit.

Mississippi judgement, which came out after Wall Street's close, was preceded by news that a Florida judge had ordered Liggett to deliver internal documents for possible use in a Florida lawsuit against U.S. tobacco companies.
